It sounds like you are deeply concerned about someone's safety, and navigating a mental health crisis with a loved one is incredibly difficult. Laws like the Baker Act allow for involuntary psychiatric examination if someone is a danger to themselves or others, though the specific name and process vary depending on where you live. To find out how to get him immediate help in your area, the safest step is to contact local emergency services or go to the nearest hospital emergency room. If you call emergency services, you can ask if they have a Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) officer available, as they are specially trained to handle mental health emergencies.

You can also call or text the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 (in the US and Canada) to speak with trained counselors. They can provide immediate guidance on the specific laws, mobile crisis teams, and resources available in your region to help him get the care he needs safely.
